title: A Gate Before the Robot: The Safety Suite as a Release Condition, a Candidate That Looks Fine and Is Not, and the Fault the Gate Cannot See

questions.question: What does the gate add to the pipeline of lesson 20-12?
options: A second check of the manifest's hash
A signature on the release
A faster install
A stage that asks whether the release is safe, before the first stage
questions.explanation: The pipeline does not know what the release does. The pipeline of 20-12 checks that a release is for this robot, intact, newer and small enough. It has no idea whether the policy inside drives into people.

questions.question: The candidate has the limiter and supervisor taken out. Which scenario passed?
options: None: an unsafe rover fails everything
S4, the lost link
S1, the empty building
All five
questions.explanation: It drives perfectly, and only the three scenarios with something in the way failed. With nothing in the way the unsafe candidate is a perfectly good rover. That is why a functional test alone proves so little.

questions.question: Why is there no flag to skip the gate?
options: A flag would slow the gate down
The compiler cannot express an optional stage
A gate that can be switched off with an argument will be, on the day it matters
Because the pipeline already has one
questions.explanation: The day somebody wants to skip the gate is the day a release is late and looks fine. Leaving no switch is the decision.

questions.question: A candidate fails only S3, which is for no hazard of the log. Does the gate pass it?
options: Yes: no hazard is failing
No: S3 is a functional scenario the robot must pass, and a robot that is safe because it never moves is not a product
Yes, with a warning in the report
Only if S1 also failed
questions.explanation: The candidate that never forgets waits for ever at a clear doorway. The gate is the whole suite, and a robot that does not do its job does not ship either.

questions.question: A candidate passes the gate and the release crashes 2 s after starting on the robot. What catches it?
options: The gate, run again on the robot
The trial of 20-06: the gate tests the policy in a simulation, the trial tests the release on a robot
The manifest check
Nothing: once past the gate a release is trusted
questions.explanation: A crash at start is a fault of the build or the image, which the simulation does not contain. The trial on the robot found it and rolled back to 1.4.2.

questions.question: Twenty robots are offered the unsafe rover. How many run it with and without the gate?
options: 0 with the gate and 20 without
20 with the gate and 20 without
0 with either: the pipeline refuses it
10 and 10
questions.explanation: The pipeline checks everything it knows to check, and the release is valid. The release was valid, fitted and booted, so the pipeline passed it to all twenty. Only the gate knew what the policy did.
